checklist.notes: The narrative and contrast examples can support A2.2, but essential directions use unsupported abstract wording such as ‘bounded events’, ‘conventionally combines’, ‘relative prominence’, ‘intended contrast’, and ‘lexical combination is intact’.
The lesson claims exactly four bounded events, but numbered event 4 contains both the rain easing and the speaker continuing, so the model and counting rule conflict.
Most narrative wording is natural. The forced indefinite collocation ‘made a decision to wait’ is grammatical but stylistically heavy, recorded as a minor issue.
Internal overlap is limited to expected target phrases and instructional frames; no external originality determination was attempted.
Narrative sequence, make a decision, and sentence stress use only the declared past-tense and word-stress prerequisite closure.
The content is English and all embedded references are in the reconstructed authority scope.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Section 1 labels exactly four events, yet ‘Finally, when the rain eased, I continued to class’ encodes two events: the rain eased and the speaker continued. Sections 2 and 4 then require exactly four, making the model’s event analysis internally false.
findings.recommendation: Remove the easing event (for example, ‘Finally, I continued to class’) or count and teach five events consistently.

findings.description: The A2.2 learner must process dense discourse and phonology metalanguage across Sections 1–4 without a simple paraphrase or L1 support, which can block access to the otherwise appropriate narrative examples.
findings.recommendation: Replace abstract labels with concrete prompts (‘What happened first?’), model stress by listening/marking, and gloss unavoidable terms.

findings.description: In this specific narrative, ‘I made a decision to wait’ sounds heavier and less idiomatic than the contextually definite ‘I made the decision to wait,’ although both preserve the target make + decision combination.
findings.recommendation: Use ‘made the decision to wait’ in the narrative while naming the general collocation as make a decision.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
